name: Namibia
summary: There is no forced heirship: freedom of testation is the first principle of Namibian wills law and is tied to Article 16 of the Constitution. Customary law governs many Black Namibians' estates. A 2018 review aims to unify succession law. Trusts and foundations were not sourced.
family_claims: Not sourced. Succession law reform is under way (2018 ministerial statement).
trust_note: Trusts: not sourced; 'yes' assumes Roman-Dutch trusts; unverified. No private-foundation law found.
open_questions: Maintenance claim of surviving spouse/dependants not sourced.
Trust law and foundations not sourced.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
Domestic trusts: likely available under the inherited common-law or Roman-Dutch tradition, but no statute or official source was read; confirm before marking yes.
